subject: Clarify: processing locations, subprocessors, and deletion timelines
messages:
From: Olivia Barnes <olivia@finnecta.com>
To: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 08:12:00 +0100
Subject: Processing locations and deletion: a few quick Qs

Hi Neha,

Thanks for taking a look at our security questionnaire. We have a short list of clarifying questions before we proceed to contract review:

- Where are customer inputs and model outputs processed for the hosted API (region names and whether any processing occurs outside customer region)?
- Which subprocessors have access to unredacted customer data (e.g., caching layers, logging, monitoring)?
- Do you do any cross-border transfers for hosted customers by default (e.g., EU->US)?
- What are your deletion guarantees for: inference inputs/outputs, KV/prefix caches, backups, and audit logs? Please include timelines.
- Is there a DPA or residency option to restrict processing to EU only?

We need concise answers and any relevant docs (DPA, data flow diagram). I can share the questionnaire as an attachment.

Thanks,
Olivia Barnes
Security & Compliance Lead
Finnecta Ltd.
Attachment: Finnecta_Security_Questionnaire_v2.pdf
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
To: Olivia Barnes <olivia@finnecta.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 18 Jun 2026 09:04:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Processing locations and deletion: a few quick Qs

Hi Olivia —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below and I've attached a one-page data flow diagram for context (redwood_data_flow_diagram.png). I've also attached our GDPR DPA draft for review (DPA_2026.pdf). Happy to jump on a short call if you'd like to walk through specifics.

1) Processing locations (hosted API):
- By default, hosted requests are routed to the nearest available Redwood-hosted region for latency and capacity (most traffic served from us-east-1 and eu-west-1).
- For customers requiring EU-only processing, we offer EU residency via a residency setting on the account or via Dedicated/Private deployments. When residency is enabled, inference, caching, and logs are kept within EU regions and are not routed to US regions for processing.

2) Subprocessors and access to data:
- Primary cloud providers: AWS (us-east-1, eu-west-1), GCP (europe-west), and Azure for selected regions.
- Edge/caching CDN: Fastly (for edge routing only; payloads are encrypted in transit).
- Observability: Datadog (ingested telemetry is redacted/aggregated; raw customer payloads are not stored there).
- Support/ops tools: PagerDuty, Sentry (error traces are redacted where possible).
- We maintain a published subprocessor list and update it as vendors change.

3) Cross-border transfers:
- If residency is NOT enabled: routing and fallbacks may result in processing outside the customer's nominal region (e.g., brief failover to US region in capacity emergencies).
- If residency is enabled (EU residency or Dedicated in EU): we do not route inference or persist logs outside the EU; support access for troubleshooting is bridged via controlled bastion sessions and is logged.

4) Deletion timelines (standard hosted):
- Inference inputs/outputs: immediately eligible for deletion on customer request; primary storage removed within 30 days.
- KV/prefix caches: in-memory by design; persistent caches that accelerate repeat prompts are encrypted and purged within 30 days of request or 7 days by default for short-term caches.
- Backups: rolling snapshots retained for up to 90 days; deletion requests trigger retention-block removal and a best-effort accelerated purge within the snapshot window.
- Audit logs/trace data: retained for 180 days by default; can be configured shorter for enterprise contracts.

Attachments: redwood_data_flow_diagram.png, DPA_2026.pdf

Next steps: I'll loop in our infra and privacy SMEs to provide the technical detail and encryption/KMS specifics.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference

- KV/prefix caches: are any customer inputs stored on disk in any temporary form (swap, local SSD) on GPU hosts?
- Cross-border support access: are support engineers able to access raw unredacted data during troubleshooting? If so, what's the approval/audit flow?
- Deletion SLA: can you commit to hard deletion from primary stores within 30 days and best-effort purge from backups within 90 days for EU residency customers in a DPA?

I'll consolidate answers into the questionnaire then share with our legal team.

Olivia

From: markus_klein@redwood.ai
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, Olivia Barnes <olivia@finnecta.com>
Cc: camila_reyes@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 19 Jun 2026 15:40:00 +0100
Subject: Re: Processing locations and deletion: a few quick Qs

Hi Olivia —

Markus from Infra here — answering the technical points directly. TL;DR: we support CMK for Private deployments today and are offering a CMK path for Hosted EU-residency customers under an enterprise addendum; caches are memory-first and not persisted to disk except transient swap under extreme OOM events (see details).

Encryption / CMK:
- Private deployments: customer-managed KMS/HSM fully supported (customer supplies keys or we integrate with the customer's KMS).
- Hosted EU-residency (enterprise): we offer an addendum to enable envelope encryption with customer-provided CMKs (via a limited KMS integration) for inference payloads and persisted artifacts. This is gated by an enterprise contract and technical onboarding.

KV/prefix caches and disk persistence:
- Our inference cache is designed to be memory-resident. On GPU hosts we prioritize in-memory KV and GPU memory for speed.
- We do not intentionally write raw customer inputs/outputs to local SSD. However, in safety-critical OOM/eviction scenarios a very small amount of encrypted swap may be used transiently; this is encrypted at rest and rotated.
- For customers that require absolutely zero swap/disk touch we can enable an explicit strictly-in-memory mode for Dedicated/Private deployments.

Support access and auditing:
- Support engineers do not have blanket access to raw customer payloads. Access is provided on a case-by-case basis and requires:
  1) escalation approval from a manager,
  2) a scoped, time-limited bastion session, and
  3) all session activity logged and retained (audit trail attached to the case).
- For EU residency customers, access is additionally restricted and must be approved by our Privacy team; access events are recorded and reviewed quarterly.

Deletion SLA and DPA wording:
- We can commit to: primary-store removal of inference inputs/outputs within 30 days of a verified deletion request for EU residency customers, and a best-effort purge from backups within 90 days. We will include explicit SLA text in the DPA addendum for Finnecta if that is required for contract signature.

Attachments included: DPA_2026.pdf (DPA draft), redwood_data_flow_diagram.png

If you want a short call to walk through the DPA wording, happy to schedule 30 minutes next week.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Director, Infrastructure
Redwood Inference
